anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Sessions serialize on hot buffer-cache pages, latches, or page pins, stalling CPU threads while they wait to read, modify, or flush pages. 
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The underlying storage subsystem cannot deliver the required read/write bandwidth or IOPS, so physical I/O latency and queue depths surge and database I/O waits dominate. 
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : The network path, listener, or connection slots are saturated or unstable, causing slow or failed connection establishment and prolonged client read/write waits. 

When all three root causes strike simultaneously, the database experiences a layered slowdown: 1) internal workers spin or block on buffer-latch waits, 2) outstanding I/O requests pile up because the storage layer is already at its throughput ceiling, and 3) client sessions struggle to connect or to consume results across an overloaded network. Observable symptoms blend and amplify—buffer-busy and page-latch waits coexist with soaring read/write latencies, while active session counts, socket queues, and retry storms grow. Application response times fluctuate wildly; some statements hang inside the engine, others time out on the wire, making the true bottleneck difficult to pinpoint. 

Causally, saturated storage keeps dirty or requested pages in flight longer, extending latch hold times and magnifying buffer contention. Prolonged execution increases session lifetime and concurrency, swelling the number of open connections and the volume of result data, which in turn stresses network and listener resources. Conversely, network stalls delay acknowledgement of commits and fetches, holding transactions open and keeping their locked and latched pages active, which further inflates buffer pressure. The compounded effect is a feedback loop: storage slowness fuels latch contention, latch contention lengthens transactions, and protracted transactions multiply network usage—all three reinforcing each other and driving the database into a severe, multi-layer performance collapse.

entry.official_definition: Write timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol write operation exceeds mysqlx_write_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network write operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
